input.body:
label: bug
file: src/ingest/parser.ts

The new Windows accounting export tool likely saves files with UTF-8 BOM encoding. Although `parseStatement` strips the UTF-8 BOM (`﻿`) from the start of the text string, it splits the input into lines before doing so (`text.split(\"\\n\")`). As a result, the BOM remains attached to the first field of the header (`\"﻿date\"`), causing `REQUIRED_COLUMNS` lookup and column-count validation (`assertShape`) to fail on row 1.
